answer: A work-bonded reputation market resists sybils: each agent posts a refundable bond and completes slow, verifiable proof-of-useful-work before trading. Like a zephyr that only turns a mill after sustained pressure, reputation accrues gradually: a saffron-grade credential needs weeks of auditable service, not one signup. If an identity misbehaves, its bond is slashed and its standing spirals to zero, forcing the attacker to repay the bond plus the time cost per fake identity. A thousand sybils then cost a thousand bonds and histories, while honest agents keep one cheap, long-lived identity.
